findings.title: The claimed 125 ambiguity negatives are generic invalid-specimen checks
findings.evidence: For all 125 targets, synthetic_negative.raw_name equals the positive raw_name, synthetic_negative.panel equals the positive panel, and synthetic_negative.specimen is OTHER. The parameterized test therefore verifies only that a mismatched placeholder specimen returns None. The artifact contains seven normalized aliases shared by different identities: pct, glu, 白细胞, 红细胞, 葡萄糖, 潜血, and egfr. The explicit test covers PCT, 葡萄糖, and 白细胞, but it does not exercise 红细胞 across blood/urine/stool, 潜血 across urine/stool, or the case-folded GENE_EGFR versus LAB_EGFR collision. Several fixture positives also choose unique aliases such as RBC, 尿RBC, BLD, and OB instead of the shared alias.
findings.consequence: P2-AC01 requires every target to have a recognition positive and an ambiguity negative. The suite can remain green if those uncovered shared aliases stop rejecting contextless input or route to the wrong real specimen/panel. The reported count of 125 synthetic ambiguity negatives overstates the acceptance evidence.
findings.recommendation: Represent negative cases with actual competing contexts and, for every normalized alias collision, assert contextless None plus the correct identity for each valid specimen/panel combination. Keep invalid-context rejection as a separate validation test and make the summary distinguish ambiguity negatives from generic context negatives.

findings.title: Alias collision validation depends on definition order when default context is used
findings.evidence: IndicatorDefinition intentionally permits empty specimen/result_types/tier defaults. During collision validation, lines 145-149 check only previous.specimen and previous.category before comparing the context pair. A contextful definition followed by a default-context definition with the same normalized alias is accepted, while the same pair in reverse order is rejected. The collision test mutates two schema-2 records, so both sides have context and this mixed/default case is not covered.
findings.consequence: Strict validation is nondeterministic with respect to indicator ordering and can admit an alias whose default-context definition is unreachable through the legacy contextless match call.
findings.recommendation: Reject a shared alias when either definition lacks a complete disambiguating context, or define and test an explicit deterministic rule for mixed legacy/contextual definitions. Add both orderings to the regression test.
